title: tracing-heuristics-sprint-checkin-2026-03-17
content:
Sprint check-in: tracing heuristics, dashboard hygiene, and a cost-focused sampling experiment

Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Omar Vasquez, Priya Patel, Liam O'Connor, Zara Ahmed, Ad-hoc: Ben Groves (SRE)

Purpose: quick weekly sync to capture what changed since last week, lock down experiment plan for sampling-to-cost mapping, and agree dashboard cleanup priorities before Friday ship window. Notes are intentionally terse — action items at the bottom.

1) Summary of current signals
- Trace ingestion: nominal volume ~ 1.1M spans/day, up 8% week-over-week. The uptick correlates with the feature flag rollout for multi-region routing (FF: multi-region-2026-03).
- Cost: raw trace storage increases felt in the nightly ingest job; observed ~12% jump in GCP egress and storage attributed to high-cardinality service tags from the new router.
- Error traces: error-span ratio unchanged (~0.7%), but error clusters from the router show longer stack traces (avg span size +1.8KB).

2) Tracing heuristics hypothesis and experiment plan
- Hypothesis: Switching to a hybrid sampling policy (route-level head-based sampling for router services + adaptive tail-sampling for downstream microservices) will reduce span volume by ~30% while preserving SLI-sensitive error traces.
- Experiment goals: 30% span reduction, <5% drop in SLI-detectable error traces, and net trace cost reduction >=25%.
- Design: two cohorts (A/B) at the routing layer for 48 hours:
  * Cohort A (control): current 1:100 head sampling + uniform reservoir tail sampling
  * Cohort B (treatment): head-sample critical routes 1:20, drop high-cardinality route tags (route.instance_id) at probe level, and enable adaptive tail-sampling with score-based priority (errors, latency > p95, new trace fingerprints)
- Metrics to collect: spans/day by service, percent of error traces detected by existing alert rules, average span size, dashboard query latency, and storage+egress delta.
- Rollback criteria: >5% missed critical alerts or >10% regression in end-to-end latency observability.

3) Dashboard & query hygiene sprint items (short list)
- Top-3 expensive queries: route-topology-summary, heavy-spans-by-tag, error-trace-explorer. Action: Omar to add index hints and reduce lookback window to 7d for non-urgent dashboards (due 2026-03-19).
- Remove redundant panels: identify panels that mirror trace counts already present in upstream aggregate dashboards. Priya will submit a PR to the dashboards repo to drop two legacy panels (due 2026-03-20).
- Query caching: enable 24h cache for read-heavy, low-churn panels (Liam to coordinate with infra; ticket OBS-357).

4) Cost telemetry notes and quick math
- Current: estimated trace unit cost (storage + egress + indexing) ~ $0.00095/span. At 1.1M spans/day this implies ~$1045/day (~$31k/month).
- Target: reduce to $0.0007/span through combined sampling and tag pruning; running numbers: at 30% fewer spans and 20% lower average span size we hit approx $0.00066/span => ~ $720/day.
- Sensitivity: each 5% error in span-reduction target changes monthly savings by ~$1.8k. We flagged this for finance review if the experiment scales.

5) Observability reliability & alerting changes
- New alert rule: trace-ingest-drop (alerts when spans/minute drops >40% relative to baseline). Reason: previous sampling misconfiguration went undetected for 6 hours in a dev region. Owner: Zara.
- Adjusted SLO for trace-service latency dashboard panels to reflect 99th pctl objective because tail latency has larger business impact for debugging.

6) Runbook snippets / debugging notes (short ops cookbook)
- If trace counts spike unexpectedly: check FFs (feature flags), examine route topology for traffic shifts, run the lightweight span-sampler simulator (local) to replay and estimate cost delta.
- To quickly validate sampling policy: 1) enable policy in canary namespace, 2) let it run for 10 minutes, 3) compare error detection rate in the canary vs control.

7) Risks / open questions
- Unknown: whether third-party SDKs (kafka-client tracing shim) will re-add high-cardinality tags after we prune them at the router. Mitigation: instrument a tag-stripping middleware in router.
- Dependency: infra needs a small config flag to let dashboards query compressed span indexes for cheaper reads (ticket OBS-360).
- UX tradeoff: some SREs prefer full fidelity for postmortem. We'll propose an archival policy that retains 100% fidelity for 30 days, sampled retention thereafter. Feedback requested.

8) Action items (owner — due)
- Omar: implement index hints and reduce lookback for heavy queries — due 2026-03-19.
- Priya: PR to drop legacy panels and note changes in dashboard changelog — due 2026-03-20.
- Liam: enable 24h query caching for listed panels and file OBS-357 — due 2026-03-21.
- Zara: create trace-ingest-drop alert with a runbook link — due 2026-03-18.
- Maya: deploy hybrid sampling to treatment cohort and monitor defined metrics; post initial 12h summary in the channel — deploy 2026-03-18 09:00 PT.
- Ben (SRE): validate that router tag-pruning middleware does not break downstream correlation — due 2026-03-19.

Appendix: quick log excerpts (sanitized)
- Example trace header: service=router routes=[eu-west,us-central] duration_ms=432 spans=12 user_id_hash=***
- Anomalous noisy tag example: route.instance_id=dc19-8f7a2b4e (unique per instance) -> affects cardinality. Plan: normalize to route.instance_bucket (8 buckets).

Decision checkpoint: reconvene Friday 2026-03-19 11:00 PT to review 48h experiment metrics and decide whether to extend or rollback.

Notes captured by: Maya Chen. Please add quick comments in-thread if you need more detail or want to reassign any tasks.
